name_note: The GTDB name matches the current literature name; older papers call the same species Propionibacterium acnes.

sentences.text: Cutibacterium acnes, renamed from Propionibacterium acnes, is a Gram-positive commensal and a major inhabitant of adult human skin, where it lives inside sebaceous follicles.
It is the most abundant bacterium of healthy sebum-rich skin sites such as the face and the back, and contributes actively to normal skin homeostasis.
Its genome encodes many products that degrade host molecules, including sialidases, neuraminidases, endoglycoceramidases, lipases and pore-forming factors.

Reviews report that loss of its relative abundance or clonal diversity accompanies acne, atopic dermatitis, rosacea and psoriasis, and that it causes implant-associated infections, notably of shoulder prostheses.
